texts: D-TGA is invariably associated with D-looping of the ventricles: B.

In simple (complete) transposition the atria are usually in their normal position (situs solitus), the heart tube loops to the right, and the aorta arises from the right ventricle, anterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery.
L-TGA, with L-looping, is congenitally corrected transposition, in which both the ventricles and the great arteries are switched.
In the picture, the swapped hotel's roller coaster loops to the right, while the mirror hotel's loops to the left.
Memory hook: D for D: the swapped hotel loops right.
